For multi-phase work (understand → design → implement → review), that often means several workflows in sequence — one per phase — so you stay in the loop between them. The quality patterns below (adversarial verify, multi-modal sweep, completeness critic, loop-until-dry) are the tools; pick what fits the task. Lean toward orchestrating with workflows and adversarially verifying your findings — unless the work is trivial or already verified. Solo only on conversational turns or trivial mechanical edits. When a reminder says ultracode is off, revert to the opt-in rule in the Workflow tool description.

Pass the script inline via `script` — do not Write it to a file first. Every invocation automatically persists its script to a file under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate on a workflow, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with `{scriptPath: "<path>"}` instead of resending the full script.

Every script must begin with `export const meta = {...}`:
  export const meta = {
    name: 'find-flaky-tests',
    description: 'Find flaky tests and propose fixes',   // one-line, shown in permission dialog
    phases: [                                            // one entry per phase() call
      { title: 'Scan', detail: 'grep test logs for retries' },
      { title: 'Fix', detail: 'one agent per flaky test' },
    ],
  }
  // script body starts here — use agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase()/log()
  phase('Scan')
  const flaky = await agent('grep CI logs for retry markers', {schema: FLAKY_SCHEMA})
  ...

The `meta` object must be a PURE LITERAL — no variables, function calls, spreads, or template interpolation. Required fields: `name`, `description`. Optional: `whenToUse` (shown in the workflow list), `phases`. Use the SAME phase titles in meta.phases as in phase() calls — titles are matched exactly; a phase() call with no matching meta entry just gets its own progress group. Add `model` to a phase entry when that phase uses a specific model override.

Script body hooks:
- agent(prompt: string, opts?: {label?: string, phase?: string, schema?: object, model?: string, effort?: string, isolation?: 'worktree', agentType?: string}): Promise<any> — spawn a subagent. Without schema, returns its final text as a string. With schema (a JSON Schema), the subagent is forced to call a StructuredOutput tool and agent() returns the validated object — no parsing needed. Returns null if the user skips the agent mid-run or the subagent dies on a terminal API error after retries (filter with .filter(Boolean)). opts.label overrides the display label. opts.phase explicitly assigns this agent to a progress group (use this inside pipeline()/parallel() stages to avoid races on the global phase() state — same phase string → same group box). opts.model overrides the model for this agent call. Default to omitting it — the agent inherits the main-loop model (the resolved session model), which is almost always correct. Only set it when you're highly confident a different tier fits the task; when unsure, omit. opts.effort overrides the reasoning effort for this agent call ('low' | 'medium' | 'high' | 'xhigh' | 'max') — omit to inherit the session effort; use 'low' for cheap mechanical stages and higher tiers only for the hardest verify/judge stages. opts.isolation: 'worktree' runs the agent in a fresh git worktree — EXPENSIVE (~200-500ms setup + disk per agent), use ONLY when agents mutate files in parallel and would otherwise conflict; the worktree is auto-removed if unchanged. opts.agentType uses a custom subagent type (e.g. 'general-purpose', 'code-reviewer') instead of the default workflow subagent — resolved from the same registry as the Agent tool; composes with schema (the custom agent's system prompt gets a StructuredOutput instruction appended).
- pipeline(items, stage1, stage2, ...): Promise<any[]> — run each item through all stages independently, NO barrier between stages. Item A can be in stage 3 while item B is still in stage 1. This is the DEFAULT for multi-stage work. Wall-clock = slowest single-item chain, not sum-of-slowest-per-stage. Every stage callback receives (prevResult, originalItem, index) — use originalItem/index in later stages to label work without threading context through stage 1's return value. A stage that throws drops that item to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- parallel(thunks: Array<() => Promise<any>>): Promise<any[]> — run tasks concurrently. This is a BARRIER: awaits all thunks before returning. A thunk that throws (or whose agent errors) resolves to `null` in the result array — the call itself never rejects, so `.filter(Boolean)` before using the results. Use ONLY when you genuinely need all results together.
- log(message: string): void — emit a progress message to the user (shown as a narrator line above the progress tree)
- phase(title: string): void — start a new phase; subsequent agent() calls are grouped under this title in the progress display
- args: any — the value passed as Workflow's `args` input, verbatim (undefined if not provided). Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values in the tool call, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — `args: ["a.ts", "b.ts"]`, not `args: "[\"a.ts\", ...]"` (a stringified list reaches the script as one string, so `args.filter`/`args.map` throw). Use this to parameterize named workflows — e.g. pass a research question, target path, or config object directly instead of via a side-channel file.
- budget: {total: number|null, spent(): number, remaining(): number} — the turn's token target from the user's "+500k"-style directive. `budget.total` is null if no target was set. `budget.spent()` returns output tokens spent this turn across the main loop and all workflows — the pool is shared, not per-workflow. `budget.remaining()` returns `max(0, total - spent())`, or `Infinity` if no target. The target is a HARD ceiling, not advisory: once `spent()` reaches `total`, further `agent()` calls throw. Use for dynamic loops: `while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) { ... }`, or static scaling: `const FLEET = budget.total ? Math.floor(budget.total / 100_000) : 5`.
- workflow(nameOrRef: string | {scriptPath: string}, args?: any): Promise<any> — run another workflow inline as a sub-step and return whatever it returns. Pass a name to invoke a saved workflow (same registry as {name: "..."}), or {scriptPath} to run a script file you Wrote earlier. The child shares this run's concurrency cap, agent counter, abort signal, and token budget — its agents appear under a "▸ name" group in /workflows and its tokens count toward budget.spent(). The args param becomes the child's `args` global. Nesting is one level only: workflow() inside a child throws. Throws on unknown name / unreadable scriptPath / child syntax error; catch to handle gracefully.

Subagents are told their final text IS the return value (not a human-facing message), so they return raw data. For structured output, use the schema option — validation happens at the tool-call layer so the model retries on mismatch.
Schemas need {type: 'object', properties: {...}} at root and required ⊆ properties; unsatisfiable ones throw at agent().

Workflow agents can reach all session-connected MCP tools via ToolSearch — schemas load on demand per agent. Caveat: interactively-authenticated MCP servers (e.g. claude.ai) may be absent in headless/cron runs.

Subagents get the same CLAUDE.md files injected at start that you did (except built-in agent types that omit them, such as Explore and Plan) — don't tell them to re-read those or paste their rules into the prompt; name the specific rule a stage needs, if any.

Scripts are plain JavaScript, NOT TypeScript — type annotations (`: string[]`), interfaces, and generics fail to parse. The script body runs in an async context — use await directly. Standard JS built-ins (JSON, Math, Array, etc.) are available — EXCEPT `Date.now()`/`Math.random()`/argless `new Date()`, which throw (they would break resume); pass timestamps in via `args`, stamp results after the workflow returns, and for randomness vary the agent prompt/label by index. No filesystem or Node.js API access.

DEFAULT TO pipeline(). Only reach for a barrier (parallel between stages) when you genuinely need ALL prior-stage results together.

A barrier is correct ONLY when stage N needs cross-item context from all of stage N-1:
- Dedup/merge across the full result set before expensive downstream work
- Early-exit if the total count is zero ("0 bugs found → skip verification entirely")
- Stage N's prompt references "the other findings" for comparison

A barrier is NOT justified by:
- "I need to flatten/map/filter first" — do it inside a pipeline stage: pipeline(items, stageA, r => transform([r]).flat(), stageB)
- "The stages are conceptually separate" — that's what pipeline() models. Separate stages ≠ synchronized stages.
- "It's cleaner code" — barrier latency is real. If 5 finders run and the slowest takes 3× the fastest, a barrier wastes 2/3 of the fast finders' idle time.

Smell test: if you wrote
  const a = await parallel(...)
  const b = transform(a)        // flatten, map, filter — no cross-item dependency
  const c = await parallel(b.map(...))
that middle transform doesn't need the barrier. Rewrite as a pipeline with the transform inside a stage. When in doubt: pipeline.

Concurrent agent() calls are capped at min(16, available CPUs - 2) per workflow — excess calls queue and run as slots free up. You can still pass 100 items to parallel()/pipeline() and they all complete; only ~10 run at any moment. Total agent count across a workflow's lifetime is capped at 1000 — a runaway-loop backstop set far above any real workflow. A single parallel()/pipeline() call accepts at most 4096 items; passing more is an explicit error, not a silent truncation.

When a barrier IS correct — dedup across all findings before expensive verification:
  const all = await parallel(DIMENSIONS.map(d => () => agent(d.prompt, {schema: FINDINGS_SCHEMA})))
  const deduped = dedupeByFileAndLine(all.filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.findings))  // <-- genuinely needs ALL at once
  const verified = await parallel(deduped.map(f => () => agent(verifyPrompt(f), {schema: VERDICT_SCHEMA})))

Loop-until-count pattern — accumulate to a target:
  const bugs = []
  while (bugs.length < 10) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length}/10 found`)
  }

Loop-until-budget pattern — scale depth to the user's "+500k" directive. Guard on budget.total: with no target set, remaining() is Infinity and the loop would run straight to the 1000-agent cap.
  const bugs = []
  while (budget.total && budget.remaining() > 50_000) {
    const result = await agent("Find bugs in this codebase.", {schema: BUGS_SCHEMA})
    bugs.push(...result.bugs)
    log(`${bugs.length} found, ${Math.round(budget.remaining()/1000)}k remaining`)
  }

Composing patterns — exhaustive review (find → dedup vs seen → diverse-lens panel → loop-until-dry):
  const seen = new Set(), confirmed = []
  let dry = 0
  while (dry < 2) {                                              // loop-until-dry
    const found = (await parallel(FINDERS.map(f => () =>          // barrier: collect all finders this round
      agent(f.prompt, {phase: 'Find', schema: BUGS})))).filter(Boolean).flatMap(r => r.bugs)
    const fresh = found.filter(b => !seen.has(key(b)))           // dedup vs ALL seen — plain code, not an agent
    if (!fresh.length) { dry++; continue }
    dry = 0; fresh.forEach(b => seen.add(key(b)))
    const judged = await parallel(fresh.map(b => () =>           // every fresh bug judged concurrently...
      parallel(['correctness','security','repro'].map(lens => () =>   // ...each by 3 distinct lenses
        agent(`Judge "${b.desc}" via the ${lens} lens — real?`, {phase: 'Verify', schema: VERDICT})))
        .then(vs => ({ b, real: vs.filter(Boolean).filter(v => v.real).length >= 2 }))))
    confirmed.push(...judged.filter(v => v.real).map(v => v.b))
  }
  return confirmed
  // dedup vs `seen`, NOT `confirmed` — else judge-rejected findings reappear every round and it never converges.

Quality patterns — common shapes; pick by task and compose freely:
- Adversarial verify: spawn N independent skeptics per finding, each prompted to REFUTE. Kill if ≥majority refute. Prevents plausible-but-wrong findings from surviving.
    const votes = await parallel(Array.from({length: 3}, () => () =>
      agent(`Try to refute: ${claim}. Default to refuted=true if uncertain.`, {schema: VERDICT})))
    const survives = votes.filter(Boolean).filter(v => !v.refuted).length >= 2
- Perspective-diverse verify: when a finding can fail in more than one way, give each verifier a distinct lens (correctness, security, perf, does-it-reproduce) instead of N identical refuters — diversity catches failure modes redundancy can't.
- Judge panel: generate N independent attempts from different angles (e.g. MVP-first, risk-first, user-first), score with parallel judges, synthesize from the winner while grafting the best ideas from runners-up. Beats one-attempt-iterated when the solution space is wide.
- Loop-until-dry: for unknown-size discovery (bugs, issues, edge cases), keep spawning finders until K consecutive rounds return nothing new. Simple counters (while count < N) miss the tail.
- Multi-modal sweep: parallel agents each searching a different way (by-container, by-content, by-entity, by-time). Each is blind to what the others surface; useful when one search angle won't find everything.
- Completeness critic: a final agent that asks "what's missing — modality not run, claim unverified, source unread?" What it finds becomes the next round of work.
- No silent caps: if a workflow bounds coverage (top-N, no-retry, sampling), `log()` what was dropped — silent truncation reads as "covered everything" when it didn't.

Scale to what the user asked for. "find any bugs" → a few finders, single-vote verify. "thoroughly audit this" or "be comprehensive" → larger finder pool, 3–5 vote adversarial pass, synthesis stage. When unsure, lean toward thoroughness for research/review/audit requests and toward brevity for quick checks.

These patterns aren't exhaustive — compose novel harnesses when the task calls for it (tournament brackets, self-repair loops, staged escalation, whatever fits).

Use this tool for multi-step orchestration where control flow should be deterministic (loops, conditionals, fan-out) rather than model-driven.

## Resume

The tool result includes a runId. To resume after a pause, kill, or script edit, relaunch with Workflow({scriptPath, resumeFromRunId}) — the longest unchanged prefix of agent() calls returns cached results instantly; the first edited/new call and everything after it runs live. Same script + same args → 100% cache hit. Before diagnosing why a completed workflow returned an empty or unexpected result, Read <transcriptDir>/journal.jsonl — it records each agent's actual return value; do not assume cached results are non-empty. Date.now()/Math.random()/new Date() are unavailable in scripts (they would break this) — stamp results after the workflow returns, or pass timestamps via args. Fallback when no journal is available: Read agent-<id>.jsonl files in the transcript directory and hand-author a continuation script.

This session has the default workflow size guideline: medium — keep workflows under 10 agents. This is a guideline, not a hard limit — follow it unless the user's prompt calls for a different scale. The user can raise or remove it with "Dynamic workflow size" in /config.

script.description: Self-contained workflow script. Must begin with `export const meta = { name, description, phases }` (pure literal, no computed values) followed by the script body using agent()/parallel()/pipeline()/phase().

name.description: Name of a predefined workflow (built-in or from .claude/workflows/). Resolves to a self-contained script.

description.description: Ignored — set the workflow description in the script's `meta` block.

title.description: Ignored — set the workflow title in the script's `meta` block.

args.description: Optional input value exposed to the script as the global `args`, verbatim. Pass arrays/objects as actual JSON values, NOT as a JSON-encoded string — a stringified list breaks `args.filter`/`args.map` in the script. Use for parameterized named workflows (e.g. a research question).

scriptPath.description: Path to a workflow script file on disk. Every Workflow invocation persists its script under the session directory and returns the path in the tool result. To iterate, edit that file with Write/Edit and re-invoke Workflow with the same `scriptPath` instead of re-sending the full script. Takes precedence over `script` and `name`.

resumeFromRunId.description: Run ID of a prior Workflow invocation to resume from. Completed agent() calls with unchanged (prompt, opts) return their cached results instantly; only edited or new calls re-run. Same-session only. Stop the prior run first (TaskStop) before resuming.

1	"""Offline light-client verification of externally supplied proof bundles.
2	
3	A proof bundle lets a client verify ledger responses without trusting the
4	serving node or holding any chain state:
5	
6	    bundle = {
7	        "source": str,
8	        "expires_at": int,            # Unix seconds
9	        "response": object,           # the attested response object
10	        "candidate": [...],           # full block list starting at genesis
11	        "proofs": [                   # optional Merkle inclusion proofs
12	            {"height": int, "proof": {height, tx_id, index, merkle_root,
13	                                      block_hash, siblings}},
14	            ...
15	        ],
16	        # Optional account-state extension: all four fields are either present
17	        # together or absent together, and state_proofs is a non-empty list.
18	        "state_root": str,            # 64 lowercase hex, anchored state root
19	        "state_height": int,          # confirmed anchor block height
20	        "state_block_hash": str,      # 64 lowercase hex anchor block hash
21	        "state_proofs": [             # account-state inclusion proofs
22	            {"height": int, "proof": {account, balance,
23	                                      confirmed_transactions, index,
24	                                      state_root, height, block_hash,
25	                                      siblings}},
26	            ...
27	        ],
28	        "signature": str,             # optional Ed25519 signature hex
29	    }
30	
31	The local trust document pins the genesis block hash and records, per source,
32	an optional Ed25519 public key with its own expiry, plus an allowlist of
33	sources accepted without signatures:
34	
35	    trust = {
36	        "genesis_hash": "<64 lowercase hex chars>",
37	        "sources": {source: {"public_key": hex, "expires_at": int}},
38	        "allowlist": {source: expires_at_int},
39	    }
40	
41	Verification, in order:
42	
43	1. **input** — bundle and trust must have the documented shape; every numeric
44	   field must be a plain (non-boolean) integer.
45	2. **auth** — the source must be trusted (a ``sources`` entry or the
46	   ``allowlist``). A source with a public key must sign the bundle; a bundle
47	   carrying a signature for a key-less source, or an unsigned bundle from a
48	   non-allowlisted source, fails.
49	3. **expired** — neither the bundle deadline nor the trust entry's deadline
50	   may have passed (``expires_at <= now`` counts as expired).
51	4. **integrity** — the signature (when required) is verified over
52	   Ed25519(sha256(sorted-compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle without
53	   ``signature``)); the candidate chain is recomputed from the pinned genesis
54	   (heights, prev_hash linkage, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
55	   signature, unique tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes, pending-only-at-tip)
56	   and the response's descriptor fields are checked against the recomputed
57	   tip descriptor ``S``.
58	5. **proof** — every proof must be unique, its tx_id/height/index and block
59	   fields must agree with the candidate block, the Merkle path must verify
60	   under the existing rules, and its block must not be the pending tip. When
61	   the state extension is present, its anchor (``state_height`` /
62	   ``state_block_hash``) must name a confirmed candidate block (integrity) and
63	   every state proof must agree with both anchor heights, the state root and
64	   the anchor hash; each account must sit at its ``index`` in the ascending
65	   account set of the anchor height's confirmed transactions, ``height`` +
66	   ``account`` pairs must be unique, and every proof must pass
67	   ``crypto.verify_account_proof`` against the bundle's anchors.
68	
69	On success :func:`verify_bundle` returns
70	``{"ok": True, "source", "S", "verified_tx_ids"}`` — plus
71	``"verified_accounts"`` (ascending) when the state extension was verified —
72	on failure ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
73	``input/auth/expired/integrity/proof``.
74	
75	:func:`verify_range_export` verifies one exported incremental range delivery
76	(the ``GET /v1/forks/sync/range/export`` document, top-level key order
77	``source, request_id, mode, expires_at, anchor, blocks, tip, attestation``)
78	offline against a caller-pinned expected anchor and the local trust document.
79	The expected anchor must strictly equal the document's ``anchor``; the
80	delivered tail is recomputed standalone from that anchor (consecutive
81	heights, prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures,
82	unique and block-ascending tx_ids, Merkle roots, block hashes,
83	pending-only-at-tip) and the closed ``tip`` summary must recompute. A
84	``plain`` export must come from an unexpired ``allowlist`` entry and carry
85	``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authenticated by key
86	version: when the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping,
87	the attestation's ``version`` selects that source's historical public key
88	(which must equal the attestation's ``public_key``); an unknown source or
89	version, or a mismatched key, is ``auth`` and a signature that fails to
90	verify is ``integrity`` — so an export signed under a since-rotated key
91	stays verifiable. A trust document without ``source_key_history`` keeps the
92	legacy rule: the source must be an unexpired ``trust.sources`` entry whose
93	pinned key matches the attestation and verifies the Ed25519 signature over
94	the SHA-256 digest of the canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message.
95	Failures map to ``input`` (structure), ``auth`` (authorization), ``expired``
96	(deadlines) and ``integrity`` (anchor/chain/signature); nothing is raised.
97	Success returns ``{"ok": True, "source", "request_id", "mode", "anchor",
98	"tip", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``verified_tx_ids`` ascending.
99	
100	:func:`verify_range_exports` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of such
101	range deliveries as one continuous chain. The first page's anchor must equal
102	the caller-pinned ``expected_anchor``; every later page's anchor must equal
103	the previous page's closed tip's ``{height, block_hash}``. Each page is
104	re-verified under the same input/auth/expired/integrity rules, transaction
105	ids are unique across the whole batch, and a pending block may only appear on
106	the last page — a broken anchor, a height jump, a duplicate transaction or any
107	block after a pending one is an ``integrity`` failure. Success returns
108	``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages", "verified_tx_ids"}`` with ``tip``
109	the last page's tip, ``pages`` the page count and ``verified_tx_ids``
110	ascending; failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one
111	of ``input/auth/expired/integrity``.
112	
113	:func:`verify_header_page` verifies one signed ``GET /v1/chain/headers``
114	page offline. The document has the exact top-level key order
115	``anchor, headers, tip, auth``: a closed ``{height, block_hash}`` anchor, an
116	ascending list of ``{height, prev_hash, merkle_root, block_hash, status}``
117	headers (no transactions), the chain descriptor S and an
118	``{key_version, signature}`` envelope. The caller pins both the anchor and
119	the tip hash; ``trust.audit_signers`` supplies the public key selected by
120	``key_version``. Key-order/type defects are ``input``; an unknown key
121	version or a failed Ed25519 verification over
122	``SHA256(UTF8("ledger-headers-v1") || canonical_json(document without
123	auth))`` is ``auth``; an anchor/tip mismatch, a recomputed header hash or
124	prev_hash link mismatch, a non-consecutive height, or a pending header
125	anywhere but the chain tail is ``integrity``. An empty page is valid only
126	when its anchor is the pinned tip. Success returns
127	``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "verified_block_hashes"}``; nothing is
128	raised for malformed input.
129	
130	:func:`verify_header_pages` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of such
131	signed header pages as one continuous chain. Every page is re-verified
132	under the exact :func:`verify_header_page` contract (key order, types,
133	signer history, domain signature, recomputed header hashes); the first
134	page's anchor must strictly equal the caller-pinned ``anchor`` and every
135	later page's anchor must equal the previous page's last header's
136	``{height, block_hash}``, so heights and prev_hash links continue across
137	the page seams and a missing, duplicated or reordered page breaks the
138	chain. Every page's ``tip`` descriptor must be field-for-field identical
139	and name the caller-pinned ``tip_hash``; the last page must reach that
140	tip. A non-final page's headers may never be empty — an empty page is
141	only ever valid as the batch's last page with its anchor being the tip —
142	and a pending header may only be the very last header of the whole batch,
143	so any page after a pending header is an ``integrity`` failure. Success
144	returns ``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "pages",
145	"verified_block_hashes"}`` with ``pages`` the page count and the hashes
146	in chain order (the anchor itself is not a header and is not included);
147	failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
148	``input`` (array/parameter shape, key order, types), ``auth`` (unknown
149	key version or a failed signature) and ``integrity`` (anchor, tip, hash,
150	link, pagination or pending-position defects). Nothing is raised.

152	:func:`verify_header_locator_page` verifies one signed
153	``POST /v1/chain/headers/locate`` page offline. The document is the same

166	signature is ``auth``; an anchor absent from the locator list, a broken

168	``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "matched_index",
169	"verified_block_hashes"}``; failure returns only ``{"ok": False,
170	"error": category}`` and nothing is raised.

172	:func:`verify_header_locator_pages` verifies an ordered, non-empty batch of
173	such signed locator pages as one continuous chain. The parameters and every

175	every page's envelope is verified under the ``ledger-headers-v1`` domain

188	``{"ok": True, "anchor", "tip", "matched_index", "pages",
189	"verified_block_hashes"}`` with ``pages`` the page count and the hashes in

191	``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` and nothing is raised.

193	:func:`advance_headers` durably checkpoints a verified header-page batch to
194	``path``. The file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document (non-ASCII written

211	nor touches the file. Loading strictly replays every stored step (shape,

214	rebuilt. Same-path advances share one lock and the new file is atomically

217	``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
218	``input/auth/integrity/state/io`` and nothing is raised.

221	checkpoint written by :func:`advance_headers`. The file is strictly

236	
237	:func:`advance` durably checkpoints a verified batch to ``path``. The
238	checkpoint file is one compact UTF-8 JSON document with the exact declared key
239	order ``generation, anchor, tip, context, state_hash`` and a single trailing
240	newline (non-ASCII written unescaped); ``generation`` starts at 1 and
241	increments per successful advance, ``anchor``/``tip`` are the batch's pinned
242	anchor and closed tip, ``context`` has the exact key order
243	``verified_at, trust, documents, verified_tx_ids`` (the ``now`` at verification,
244	the trust document and the re-verifiable batch verbatim) and ``state_hash`` is
245	the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact) JSON of the other four fields.
246	The first advance requires a legal ``anchor``; later advances accept ``None``
247	(continue from the stored tip) or the stored tip's ``{height, block_hash}``.
248	Verification itself is :func:`verify_range_exports` unchanged. Same-path
249	advances share one lock and the new file is atomically replaced into place; a
250	failed verification never bumps the generation. An existing checkpoint is
251	strictly reloaded (key order, types, state hash and a context replay at its
252	``verified_at``); any mismatch is a ``state`` failure and the file is never
253	truncated or rebuilt. Failures return only ``{"ok": False, "error":
254	category}`` with category one of
255	``input/auth/expired/integrity/state/io``; success appends the new
256	``generation`` as the final result key.
257	
258	Every successful :func:`advance` also maintains a generation-history sidecar
259	at ``path + ".history"``: one compact UTF-8 JSON document (same serialization
260	rules as the checkpoint) with the exact top-level key order
261	``v, base, records, head``. ``v`` is 1; ``base`` is ``{generation, hash}``
262	naming the generation *before* the first retained record; each record is
263	``{checkpoint, prev, hash}`` where ``checkpoint`` is the persisted five-key
264	checkpoint document, ``prev`` is the previous record's hash (the first
265	record's is ``base.hash``) and ``hash`` is
266	``SHA256(ASCII(prev) || canonical_json(checkpoint))``; ``head`` is the last
267	record's hash. Record generations run consecutively from
268	``base.generation + 1``. A fresh path starts from ``base = {0, Z}`` (Z = 64
269	zeros); a pre-existing generation-``g`` checkpoint without a sidecar is
270	treated as ``base = {g-1, Z}`` with that checkpoint as the first record, and
271	later advances append. Both files are written under the same per-path lock as
272	one transaction: an ``io`` failure restores the original bytes best-effort
273	(a failed compensation surfaces as ``state`` on the next read); crash
274	atomicity across the two files is not guaranteed.
275	
276	:func:`history` reads (and prunes) the sidecar. ``history(path)`` returns
277	``{"ok", "base", "record", "head", "kept"}`` with ``record`` the last
278	generation's record and ``kept`` null; ``generation=`` selects one retained
279	generation (an absent one is a ``state`` failure). ``keep=n`` (mutually
280	exclusive with ``generation``; both must be non-boolean positive integers)
281	retains only the last ``min(n, count)`` records: when nothing is pruned the
282	file's bytes are untouched, otherwise ``base`` becomes the last pruned
283	record's ``{generation, hash}`` and the sidecar is rewritten (the checkpoint
284	file itself never changes). Loading replays every retained generation —
285	shape, state hash, context replay and anchor continuity — so any tampering
286	is a ``state`` failure; a missing or unreadable sidecar is ``io``.
287	
288	:func:`export_history` exports the retained sidecar pages as signed,
289	offline-verifiable page documents. ``export_history(path, key, after=None,
290	limit=50, trust_path=None)`` strictly reloads both the checkpoint and its
291	sidecar under the shared per-path lock and returns one page with the exact key
292	order ``base, records, next, head, checkpoint, auth``: ``base``/``records``
293	are the sidecar's own documents (nested key orders unchanged), ``head`` the
294	sidecar head, ``checkpoint`` the persisted five-key checkpoint (identical to
295	the last retained record's), ``next`` the page's last record generation when
296	another page follows or ``null`` on the final page, and ``auth`` is
297	``{public_key, signature}`` where the Ed25519 signature is made by the 64-hex
298	seed ``key`` over the SHA-256 of the canonical (sorted, compact,
299	unescaped-non-ASCII) JSON of the page with ``auth`` removed. ``after`` is
300	``None`` (start after ``base``) or a non-boolean non-negative integer naming
301	either ``base.generation`` or a non-last retained generation; ``limit`` is a
302	non-boolean integer in 1..200. Bad arguments are ``input``, a missing or
303	unreadable file ``io`` and a corrupt checkpoint/sidecar or unmatched cursor
304	``state``. With ``trust_path`` set to a signer log (see
305	:func:`history_trust`), the log is strictly loaded first (a missing log is
306	``io`` and a corrupt one ``state``) and the page is truncated to the longest
307	prefix, starting at the cursor, whose checkpoints all carry the same key
308	active at their ``verified_at``: it stops just before the first record that
309	would straddle an authorization boundary and sets ``next`` (non-null) so the
310	following page continues there. The seed ``key`` must derive to the public
311	key covering that whole span — an unknown or revoked covering key is an
312	``auth`` failure. A page ending exactly at the retained tail still closes
313	with ``next: null``.
314	
315	:func:`verify_history` verifies an ordered, non-empty list of such pages
316	offline against one pinned 64-hex Ed25519 ``public_key``. Every page must have
317	the exact key order and nested types; ``base``, ``head``, ``checkpoint`` and
318	the signing public key must be identical on every page; each Ed25519 signature
319	must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. Records must run
320	consecutively from ``base.generation + 1`` and link across page seams through
321	each page's ``next`` (a non-final page's ``next`` is its last record
322	generation), every record hash is recomputed and every checkpoint is replayed
323	(state hash plus the stored batch context) with anchor continuity. The final
324	page alone carries ``next: null``, its last record's hash must equal ``head``
325	and its checkpoint must equal the page checkpoint; missing, duplicate or
326	reordered pages and any tampering are rejected. Success is ``{"ok": True}``;
327	failure is ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` with category one of
328	``input`` (structure/types), ``auth`` (pinned key or signature) and
329	``integrity`` (chaining, pagination or checkpoint replay); nothing is raised.
330	
331	:func:`verify_history_trust` verifies the same pages against a signer
332	rotation/revocation log instead of one pinned page key, so each page's
333	``auth.public_key`` may differ. The ``trust`` document has the exact key
334	order ``root, records, head``: ``root`` is a 64-hex Ed25519 key that must
335	equal the pinned ``root`` argument; every non-empty record has the exact key
336	order ``at, key, status, prev, signature`` with ``at`` a plain
337	(non-boolean) positive strictly-ascending integer, ``key``/``prev`` 64
338	lowercase hex, ``status`` exactly ``active``/``revoked`` and ``signature``
339	128 lowercase hex. The first ``prev`` is 64 zeros, every later one is the
340	previous record's canonical-JSON SHA-256 and ``head`` is the last record's
341	hash; each certificate is the root key's Ed25519 signature over the
342	SHA-256 of the record's canonical JSON with ``signature`` removed. An
343	``active`` record authorizes ``key`` from its ``at`` until the next record;
344	a ``revoked`` one withdraws it until a later ``active``. A page must name
345	the single key active at every checkpoint ``verified_at`` it carries — a
346	page straddling an authorization boundary is rejected — and its signature
347	must verify over the auth-less canonical page digest. All page structure,
348	chaining, pagination and checkpoint-replay rules stay identical to
349	:func:`verify_history`. Failures map to ``input`` (missing/extra/reordered
350	keys, wrong types or hex), ``auth`` (root mismatch, a bad certificate or
351	page signature, an unknown or revoked page key) and ``integrity`` (``at``
352	not ascending, a bad ``prev``/``head``, a boundary crossing, or any
353	record/pagination/checkpoint-replay defect); nothing is raised and success
354	is ``{"ok": True}``.
355	
356	:func:`history_trust` persists such a signer log at its own file path.
357	``history_trust(path)`` strictly loads and returns the ``{root, records,
358	head}`` document; a missing file is an ``io`` failure and any damaged log a
359	``state`` failure. ``history_trust(path, root_seed, at, key, status)``

361	or all absent — with ``root_seed`` a 64-hex Ed25519 seed (its public key is
362	the log root), ``at`` a non-boolean positive integer, ``key`` a 64-hex public
363	key and ``status`` ``active``/``revoked``. A fresh log must open with
364	``active``; ``at`` must strictly ascend; a ``revoked`` entry must name the
365	currently active key; re-appending the current tail's ``at``/``key``/
366	``status`` is idempotent. A seed whose root does not match the existing log
367	is ``auth``; bad argument shapes are ``input``; read-missing and read/write
368	``io``. The file uses the same compact-UTF-8/unescaped/single-trailing-
369	newline serialization and atomic per-path-locked replace as the checkpoint
370	files, and a failed write restores the original bytes best-effort.

434	def canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle: dict) -> bytes:
435	    """Sorted, compact UTF-8 JSON of the bundle with its signature removed.
436	
437	    This is the exact byte document whose SHA-256 the source signs, so signers
438	    and verifiers always agree regardless of incoming key order. The
439	    serialization mirrors :func:`ledger.crypto.canonical_message`: sorted keys,
440	    compact separators, UTF-8 bytes.
441	    """
442	    unsigned = {key: value for key, value in bundle.items() if key != "signature"}
443	    return json.dumps(
444	        unsigned, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":")
445	    ).encode("utf-8")

449	    """The 32-byte SHA-256 digest covered by a bundle Ed25519 signature."""
450	    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_bundle_bytes(bundle)).digest()

453	def verify_bundle(bundle: object, trust: object, now: float | None = None) -> dict:
454	    """Verify an offline proof bundle against the local trust document.
455	
456	    Returns ``{"ok": True, "source": ..., "S": ..., "verified_tx_ids": [...]}``
457	    on success — extended bundles also carry ``"verified_accounts"`` — or
458	    ``{"ok": False, "error": category}`` on failure. Never raises for
459	    malformed input: every defect maps to one of the five categories.
460	    """
461	    current = time.time() if now is None else now
462	    try:
463	        source, candidate = _validate_inputs(bundle, trust)
464	        _authenticate(bundle, trust, source, current)
465	        blocks_raw = candidate["blocks"] if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
466	        blocks = _recompute_chain(blocks_raw, trust)
467	        descriptor = _tip_descriptor(blocks)
468	        _check_candidate_summary(candidate, descriptor)
469	        _check_response(bundle["response"], descriptor)
470	        has_state = "state_root" in bundle
471	        if has_state:
472	            _check_state_anchor(bundle, blocks)
473	        verified_ids = _verify_proofs(bundle["proofs"], blocks)
474	        verified_accounts = (
475	            _verify_state_proofs(bundle, blocks) if has_state else None
476	        )
477	    except _Failure as failure:
478	        return {"ok": False, "error": failure.category}
479	    except Exception:
480	        # Defensive: structurally unforeseeable inputs must report rather than
481	        # crash the verifying process.
482	        return {"ok": False, "error": ERR_INPUT}
483	    result = {
484	        "ok": True,
485	        "source": source,
486	        "S": descriptor,
487	        "verified_tx_ids": verified_ids,
488	    }
489	    if verified_accounts is not None:
490	        result["verified_accounts"] = verified_accounts

497	def _validate_inputs(bundle: object, trust: object) -> tuple[str, object]:
498	    """Structural validation of bundle and trust.
499	
500	    Returns ``(source, candidate)`` where ``candidate`` is the raw candidate
501	    value (a bare block list or an export-format object carrying ``blocks``).
502	    The bundle itself is never mutated: the signature covers it verbatim.
503	    """
504	    if not isinstance(bundle, dict):
505	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
506	    for field in ("source", "expires_at", "response", "candidate", "proofs"):
507	        if field not in bundle:
508	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
509	    source = bundle["source"]
510	    if not isinstance(source, str) or not source:
511	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
512	    if not _is_int(bundle["expires_at"]):
513	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
514	    # The response is itself a JSON object; anything else cannot be checked
515	    # against the recomputed chain descriptor.
516	    if not isinstance(bundle["response"], dict):
517	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
518	    candidate = bundle["candidate"]
519	    blocks_raw = candidate.get("blocks") if isinstance(candidate, dict) else candidate
520	    if not isinstance(blocks_raw, list) or not blocks_raw:
521	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
522	    if not isinstance(bundle["proofs"], list):
523	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
524	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
525	    if signature is not None and (not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature):
526	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
527	    _validate_state_fields(bundle)
528	
529	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
530	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
531	    if not crypto.is_hex64(trust.get("genesis_hash")):
532	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
533	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
534	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
535	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
536	    for name, entry in sources.items():
537	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
538	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
539	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
540	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
541	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
542	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
543	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
544	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
545	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
546	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
547	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
548	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
549	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
550	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
551	    return source, candidate

554	def _validate_state_fields(bundle: dict) -> None:
555	    """Structural validation of the optional account-state extension.
556	
557	    The four state fields are all-or-nothing; when present, ``state_root`` and
558	    ``state_block_hash`` must be 64-char lowercase hex, ``state_height`` a
559	    non-boolean non-negative integer and ``state_proofs`` a non-empty list.
560	    Every item must carry exactly ``{height, proof}`` and every proof document
561	    exactly the eight documented keys with the right JSON types. Only shape
562	    and type are judged here — domain defects (bad hex, negative balances,
563	    illegal directions) are reported later as integrity/proof failures.
564	    """
565	    present = [field for field in STATE_FIELDS if field in bundle]
566	    if not present:
567	        return
568	    if len(present) != len(STATE_FIELDS):
569	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
570	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_root"]):
571	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
572	    if not _is_int(bundle["state_height"]) or bundle["state_height"] < 0:
573	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
574	    if not crypto.is_hex64(bundle["state_block_hash"]):
575	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
576	    state_proofs = bundle["state_proofs"]
577	    if not isinstance(state_proofs, list) or not state_proofs:
578	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
579	    for item in state_proofs:
580	        if not isinstance(item, dict) or set(item) != {"height", "proof"}:
581	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
582	        if not _is_int(item["height"]):
583	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
584	        proof = item["proof"]
585	        if not isinstance(proof, dict) or set(proof) != _STATE_PROOF_KEYS:
586	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
587	        if not isinstance(proof["account"], str) or not proof["account"]:
588	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
589	        if not _is_int(proof["balance"]):
590	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
591	        transactions = proof["confirmed_transactions"]
592	        if not isinstance(transactions, list) or any(
593	            not isinstance(tx_id, str) for tx_id in transactions
594	        ):
595	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
596	        if not _is_int(proof["index"]):
597	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
598	        if not isinstance(proof["state_root"], str):
599	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
600	        if not _is_int(proof["height"]):
601	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
602	        if not isinstance(proof["block_hash"], str):
603	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
604	        if not isinstance(proof["siblings"], list):
605	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)

609	
610	
611	def _authenticate(
612	    bundle: dict, trust: dict, source: str, now: float
613	) -> None:
614	    """Check source trust, every deadline and the optional Ed25519 signature."""
615	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
616	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
617	    source_entry = sources.get(source)
618	    allowlist_expiry = allowlist.get(source)
619	    if source_entry is None and allowlist_expiry is None:
620	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
621	
622	    # All deadlines are checked before any signature work: an expired,
623	    # correctly-signed bundle is still unusable. A source listed in both
624	    # ``sources`` and ``allowlist`` is bound by both deadlines.
625	    if bundle["expires_at"] <= now:
626	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
627	    if source_entry is not None and source_entry["expires_at"] <= now:
628	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
629	    if allowlist_expiry is not None and allowlist_expiry <= now:
630	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
631	
632	    public_key = source_entry.get("public_key") if source_entry else None
633	    signature = bundle.get("signature")
634	    if public_key is not None:
635	        # A keyed source must sign: a missing signature cannot authenticate.
636	        if signature is None:
637	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
638	        if not crypto.verify_signature(
639	            public_key, bundle_signing_digest(bundle), signature
640	        ):
641	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
642	        return
643	    # The source reached this point only through the allowlist (every sources
644	    # entry pins a key). An unsigned allowlisted bundle is therefore accepted;
645	    # a signature with no pinned key to check it against is meaningless.
646	    if signature is not None:
647	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)

654	    tip = blocks[-1]

656	        "tip_hash": tip.block_hash,
657	        "height": tip.height,

663	def _recompute_chain(candidate_raw: list, trust: dict) -> list[Block]:
664	    """Recompute and validate the whole candidate chain from the pinned genesis.
665	
666	    Mirrors the node's own candidate rules except the endowment balance replay
667	    (an offline client holds no balance convention): genesis anchor, heights,
668	    prev_hash linkage, per-transaction tx_id and Ed25519 signatures, unique
669	    tx_id-sorted transactions, Merkle roots, block hashes and the
670	    pending-only-at-tip rule. Every field is checked on the *raw* JSON value so
671	    coercions such as ``"1"`` or ``1.0`` heights are rejected outright; such
672	    type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height, non-positive or
673	    non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while recomputation
674	    mismatches stay ``integrity``.
675	    """
676	    blocks: list[Block] = []
677	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
678	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(candidate_raw):
679	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
680	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
681	        height = block_raw.get("height")
682	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
683	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
684	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
685	        status = block_raw.get("status")
686	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
687	        # A height of the wrong type or sign is a field-type defect (input),
688	        # not a chain mismatch: strings, floats and booleans must never be
689	        # coerced into plausible integers before the linkage checks below.
690	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
691	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
692	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
693	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
694	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
695	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
696	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
697	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
698	        if height != position:
699	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
700	        expected_prev = (
701	            GENESIS_PREV_HASH if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
702	        )
703	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
704	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
705	        if position == 0:
706	            # Genesis must be the exact block the client pinned: confirmed,
707	            # empty, and carrying the trusted hash (recomputed below too).
708	            if status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or txs_raw:
709	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
710	            if block_hash != trust["genesis_hash"]:
711	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
712	        elif position < len(candidate_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
713	            # A pending block may only sit at the chain tip.
714	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
715	
716	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
717	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
718	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
719	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
720	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
721	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
722	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
723	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
724	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
725	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
726	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
727	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
728	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
729	            # Same rule as the block height: the raw amount must already be a
730	            # non-boolean positive integer — never a coercible string, float
731	            # or bool — so a domain/type defect is reported as input.
732	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
733	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
734	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
735	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
736	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
737	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
738	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
739	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
740	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
741	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
742	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
743	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
744	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
745	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
746	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
747	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
748	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
749	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
750	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
751	        if recomputed != block_hash:
752	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
753	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
754	        # the comparison decisions above.
755	        try:
756	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
757	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
758	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
759	    return blocks

766	    supplied ``tip_hash/height/length/status`` must equal the recomputed tip

777	    """Every descriptor field present in the response must equal the tip's.
778	
779	    A response carrying none of the descriptor fields cannot be bound to the
780	    recomputed chain at all, so it is rejected rather than vacuously accepted.
781	    """

792	def _check_state_anchor(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> None:
793	    """Bind the state extension's anchor to the recomputed candidate chain.
794	
795	    ``state_height`` must name a confirmed candidate block whose hash equals
796	    ``state_block_hash``; an unknown height, a pending block or a hash
797	    mismatch is an integrity failure. Every state-proof item and document
798	    must agree with both anchor heights, the bundle's state root and the
799	    anchor block hash.
800	    """
801	    height = bundle["state_height"]
802	    state_root = bundle["state_root"]
803	    block_hash = bundle["state_block_hash"]
804	    if height >= len(blocks):
805	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
806	    block = blocks[height]
807	    if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED or block.block_hash != block_hash:
808	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
809	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
810	        proof = item["proof"]
811	        if item["height"] != height or proof["height"] != height:
812	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
813	        if proof["state_root"] != state_root or proof["block_hash"] != block_hash:
814	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)

817	# -- stage 5: proofs ----------------------------------------------------------
818	
819	
820	def _verify_proofs(proofs_raw: list, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
821	    """Validate uniqueness and cross-block consistency of every proof.
822	
823	    Each entry is ``{"height": int, "proof": doc}`` and the proof document
824	    follows the server shape ``{height, tx_id, index, merkle_root, block_hash,
825	    siblings}``. Proofs for the pending tip are forbidden. The verified
826	    transaction ids are returned sorted ascending.
827	    """
828	    verified: list[str] = []
829	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
830	    for item in proofs_raw:
831	        if not isinstance(item, dict):
832	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
833	        height = item.get("height")
834	        proof = item.get("proof")
835	        if not _is_int(height) or not isinstance(proof, dict):
836	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
837	        if height < 0 or height >= len(blocks):
838	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
839	        block = blocks[height]
840	        if block.height != height:
841	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
842	        # Pending tips never carry trustworthy proofs.
843	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
844	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
845	
846	        tx_id = proof.get("tx_id")
847	        index = proof.get("index")
848	        if not crypto.is_hex64(tx_id) or not _is_int(index):
849	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
850	        # The item height and the proof document's own fields must agree with
851	        # the candidate block they claim inclusion in.
852	        if proof.get("height") != height or proof.get("block_hash") != block.block_hash:
853	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
854	        if proof.get("merkle_root") != block.merkle_root:
855	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
856	        if index < 0 or index >= len(block.transactions):
857	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
858	        if block.transactions[index].tx_id != tx_id:
859	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
860	
861	        key = (height, tx_id)
862	        if key in seen:
863	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
864	        seen.add(key)
865	
866	        if not crypto.verify_merkle_proof(
867	            tx_id,
868	            proof.get("siblings"),
869	            block.merkle_root,
870	            block.block_hash,
871	            block.block_hash,
872	        ):
873	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
874	        verified.append(tx_id)
875	    return sorted(verified)
876	
877	
878	def _verify_state_proofs(bundle: dict, blocks: list[Block]) -> list[str]:
879	    """Verify every account-state proof against the bundle's state anchor.
880	
881	    The anchor's confirmed transactions determine the ascending account set;
882	    each proof's ``account`` must belong to it and its ``index`` must be the
883	    account's position in that ordering. ``height`` + ``account`` pairs must
884	    be unique. Every proof is then checked with
885	    :func:`crypto.verify_account_proof` against the bundle's ``state_root``,
886	    ``state_height`` and ``state_block_hash``; any failure — an illegal
887	    direction or hash, a forged leaf, an illegal self-pair, a malformed
888	    sibling path — is a proof failure. Returns the verified accounts sorted
889	    ascending.
890	    """
891	    height = bundle["state_height"]
892	    # The account set of the anchor height: every account touched by a
893	    # confirmed transaction up to and including the anchor block, ascending.
894	    accounts: set[str] = set()
895	    for block in blocks[: height + 1]:
896	        if block.status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
897	            continue
898	        for tx in block.transactions:
899	            accounts.add(tx.sender)
900	            accounts.add(tx.recipient)
901	    position = {account: index for index, account in enumerate(sorted(accounts))}
902	
903	    verified: list[str] = []
904	    seen: set[tuple] = set()
905	    for item in bundle["state_proofs"]:
906	        proof = item["proof"]
907	        account = proof["account"]
908	        expected = position.get(account)
909	        # An account outside the anchor's set, or an index that is not the
910	        # account's ascending position (including out-of-range), is a proof
911	        # failure.
912	        if expected is None or proof["index"] != expected:
913	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
914	        key = (item["height"], account)
915	        if key in seen:
916	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
917	        seen.add(key)
918	        if not crypto.verify_account_proof(
919	            proof,
920	            bundle["state_root"],
921	            height,
922	            bundle["state_block_hash"],
923	        ):
924	            raise _Failure(ERR_PROOF)
925	        verified.append(account)
926	    return sorted(verified)

1019	    attestation``); ``expected_anchor`` is the caller-pinned
1020	    ``{height, block_hash}`` the first page's anchor must strictly equal;
1021	    ``trust`` is the local trust document applied to every page.

1024	    ``expected_anchor``, and every later page's anchor must strictly equal the
1025	    previous page's closed ``tip`` reduced to ``{height, block_hash}`` — which
1026	    also rejects a height jump or a fork at the seam. Transaction ids must be

1035	    ``input/auth/expired/integrity``. Never raises for malformed input.

1054	            # every later page's previous tip — so a broken seam or a height

1082	        "ok": True,
1083	        "anchor": first_anchor,

1093	    """Verify one range page, returning ``(anchor, tip, verified_tx_ids)``.

1096	    :func:`verify_range_exports` (a batch chaining each page's tip into the
1097	    next page's expected anchor). Raises :class:`_Failure` with the public
1098	    error category on every defect.

1173	def _validate_range_trust(trust: object) -> None:
1174	    """Structural validation of the trust document's ``sources``/``allowlist``.
1175	
1176	    Mirrors the bundle verifier's trust rules; a ``genesis_hash`` is not
1177	    required here because the caller pins the range anchor directly. The
1178	    optional GET /v1/trust ``source_key_history`` mapping is validated too:
1179	    each source maps to a non-empty ascending array of
1180	    ``{version, public_key, activated_event_id}`` items whose versions are
1181	    dense from 1 with strictly ascending activation ids, both numeric fields
1182	    non-boolean positive integers and the public key 64 lowercase hex.
1183	    """
1184	    if not isinstance(trust, dict):
1185	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1186	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1187	    if not isinstance(sources, dict):
1188	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1189	    for name, entry in sources.items():
1190	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not isinstance(entry, dict):
1191	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1192	        if not _is_int(entry.get("expires_at")):
1193	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1194	        public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1195	        # Ed25519 public keys are 32 raw bytes, i.e. 64 hex characters.
1196	        if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1197	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1198	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1199	    if not isinstance(allowlist, dict):
1200	        raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1201	    for name, expires_at in allowlist.items():
1202	        if not isinstance(name, str) or not name or not _is_int(expires_at):
1203	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1204	    history = trust.get("source_key_history")
1205	    if history is not None:
1206	        if not isinstance(history, dict):
1207	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1208	        for name, entries in history.items():
1209	            if not isinstance(name, str) or not name:
1210	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1211	            if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
1212	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1213	            last_activated = None
1214	            for position, entry in enumerate(entries):
1215	                if not isinstance(entry, dict) or set(entry) != set(
1216	                    _HISTORY_ENTRY_KEYS
1217	                ):
1218	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1219	                version = entry.get("version")
1220	                public_key = entry.get("public_key")
1221	                activated = entry.get("activated_event_id")
1222	                # Versions are dense from 1; both numeric fields are plain
1223	                # (non-boolean) positive integers.
1224	                if not _is_int(version) or version != position + 1:
1225	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1226	                if not isinstance(public_key, str) or not _HEX32_RE.fullmatch(public_key):
1227	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1228	                if not _is_int(activated) or activated < 1:
1229	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1230	                if last_activated is not None and activated <= last_activated:
1231	                    raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1232	                last_activated = activated

1240	def _authenticate_range_export(document: dict, trust: dict, now: float) -> None:
1241	    """Check mode-specific source authorization and every deadline.
1242	
1243	    A ``plain`` export is only acceptable from an allowlisted source and must
1244	    carry ``attestation: null``. An ``attested`` export is authorized one of
1245	    two ways:
1246	
1247	    * the trust document carries a ``source_key_history`` mapping (the new
1248	      rule): the source must appear in the mapping — the historical public key
1249	      matching and signature verification happen by attestation version in
1250	      :func:`_verify_range_attestation`; the trust ``sources`` entry and its
1251	      deadline play no role, so a delivery signed under a since-rotated or
1252	      revoked key still authenticates as long as the document itself is
1253	      unexpired;
1254	    * the mapping is absent (the legacy rule): the source must be a
1255	      ``sources`` entry whose unexpired deadline is checked.
1256	
1257	    All deadlines are checked before any integrity work: an expired,
1258	    correctly-signed export is still unusable.
1259	    """
1260	    source = document["source"]
1261	    mode = document["mode"]
1262	    sources = trust.get("sources", {})
1263	    allowlist = trust.get("allowlist", {})
1264	    if mode == "plain":
1265	        if source not in allowlist:
1266	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1267	        # A plain export carrying an attestation is not a plain delivery.
1268	        if document["attestation"] is not None:
1269	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1270	    elif _has_key_history(trust):
1271	        # Historical-key authorization: the source (and later the attestation
1272	        # version) must resolve in the mapping; the current registry entry is
1273	        # deliberately not consulted.
1274	        if source not in trust["source_key_history"]:
1275	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1276	    elif source not in sources:
1277	        raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1278	
1279	    if document["expires_at"] <= now:
1280	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1281	    if mode == "plain":
1282	        if allowlist[source] <= now:
1283	            raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)
1284	    elif not _has_key_history(trust) and sources[source]["expires_at"] <= now:
1285	        # Legacy rule only: the pinned registry entry's own deadline applies.
1286	        raise _Failure(ERR_EXPIRED)

1289	def _recompute_range_tail(anchor: dict, blocks_raw: list) -> list[Block]:
1290	    """Recompute and validate the delivered tail standalone from the anchor.
1291	
1292	    Mirrors the node's own range-tail rules: heights run consecutively from
1293	    ``anchor.height + 1``, the first ``prev_hash`` is the anchor hash and
1294	    later ones link internally, every transaction's tx_id and Ed25519
1295	    signature verifies, tx_ids are unique across the tail and ascending
1296	    inside each block, Merkle roots and block hashes recompute, and a pending
1297	    block may only sit at the tail tip. Every field is checked on the *raw*
1298	    JSON value; type/domain defects (non-integer or negative height,
1299	    non-positive or non-integer amount) are reported as ``input``, while
1300	    recomputation mismatches stay ``integrity``.
1301	    """
1302	    blocks: list[Block] = []
1303	    seen_tx_ids: set[str] = set()
1304	    for position, block_raw in enumerate(blocks_raw):
1305	        if not isinstance(block_raw, dict):
1306	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1307	        height = block_raw.get("height")
1308	        prev_hash = block_raw.get("prev_hash")
1309	        merkle_root = block_raw.get("merkle_root")
1310	        block_hash = block_raw.get("block_hash")
1311	        status = block_raw.get("status")
1312	        txs_raw = block_raw.get("transactions")
1313	        # Same rule as the whole-chain recomputation: a height of the wrong
1314	        # type or sign is a field-type defect (input), never coerced.
1315	        if not _is_int(height) or height < 0:
1316	            raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1317	        if not isinstance(prev_hash, str):
1318	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1319	        if not crypto.is_hex64(merkle_root) or not crypto.is_hex64(block_hash):
1320	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1321	        if status not in ("pending", "confirmed") or not isinstance(txs_raw, list):
1322	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1323	        if height != anchor["height"] + 1 + position:
1324	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1325	        expected_prev = (
1326	            anchor["block_hash"] if position == 0 else blocks[position - 1].block_hash
1327	        )
1328	        if prev_hash != expected_prev:
1329	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1330	        if position < len(blocks_raw) - 1 and status != STATUS_CONFIRMED:
1331	            # A pending block may only sit at the tail tip.
1332	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1333	
1334	        tx_ids: list[str] = []
1335	        for raw_tx in txs_raw:
1336	            if not isinstance(raw_tx, dict):
1337	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1338	            sender = raw_tx.get("from")
1339	            recipient = raw_tx.get("to")
1340	            amount = raw_tx.get("amount")
1341	            signature = raw_tx.get("signature")
1342	            stored_tx_id = raw_tx.get("tx_id")
1343	            if not isinstance(sender, str) or not sender:
1344	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1345	            if not isinstance(recipient, str) or not recipient:
1346	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1347	            # The raw amount must already be a non-boolean positive integer —
1348	            # never a coercible string, float or bool.
1349	            if not _is_int(amount) or amount <= 0:
1350	                raise _Failure(ERR_INPUT)
1351	            if not isinstance(signature, str) or not signature:
1352	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1353	            message = crypto.canonical_message(sender, recipient, amount)
1354	            tx_id = crypto.compute_tx_id(message)
1355	            if stored_tx_id != tx_id or not crypto.is_hex64(stored_tx_id):
1356	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1357	            if not crypto.verify_signature(sender, message, signature):
1358	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1359	            if tx_id in seen_tx_ids:
1360	                raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1361	            seen_tx_ids.add(tx_id)
1362	            tx_ids.append(tx_id)
1363	        if tx_ids != sorted(tx_ids):
1364	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1365	        if crypto.merkle_root(tx_ids) != merkle_root:
1366	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1367	        recomputed = compute_block_hash(height, prev_hash, merkle_root)
1368	        if recomputed != block_hash:
1369	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
1370	        # Parsed only after every raw field has checked out; never trusted for
1371	        # the comparison decisions above.
1372	        try:
1373	            blocks.append(Block.from_dict(block_raw))
1374	        except (KeyError, TypeError, ValueError):
1375	            raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY) from None
1376	    return blocks

1397	def _verify_range_attestation(document: dict, trust: dict) -> None:
1398	    """Verify the attested export's Ed25519 signature under the pinned key.
1399	
1400	    Two rules, selected by the trust document:
1401	
1402	    * with ``source_key_history`` present, the attestation's ``version``
1403	      selects the source's historical public key; the source not appearing in
1404	      the mapping, or the attestation version not being one of its dense
1405	      versions, is an authorization failure (``auth``), as is a mismatch
1406	      between the attestation's ``public_key`` and that historical key. The
1407	      Ed25519 signature is then checked over the SHA-256 digest of the
1408	      canonical ``ledger-sync-range-v1`` message — a wrong signature is an
1409	      integrity failure. The attestation's version is already structurally
1410	      guaranteed to be a positive integer.
1411	    * without the mapping (legacy rule), the attestation's ``public_key``
1412	      must be exactly the key the trust document pins in ``sources`` for the
1413	      source (a mismatched credential is an authorization failure) and the
1414	      same signature check follows.
1415	    """
1416	    source = document["source"]
1417	    attestation = document["attestation"]
1418	    if _has_key_history(trust):
1419	        history = trust["source_key_history"].get(source)
1420	        if history is None:
1421	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1422	        version = attestation["version"]
1423	        # Versions are structurally guaranteed dense from 1, so a valid
1424	        # version simply indexes the ascending history.
1425	        if version < 1 or version > len(history):
1426	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1427	        pinned = history[version - 1]["public_key"]
1428	        if attestation["public_key"] != pinned:
1429	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1430	    else:
1431	        pinned = trust.get("sources", {})[source]["public_key"]
1432	        if attestation["public_key"] != pinned:
1433	            raise _Failure(ERR_AUTH)
1434	    message = attested_range_message(
1435	        source,
1436	        document["request_id"],
1437	        document["expires_at"],
1438	        document["anchor"],
1439	        document["blocks"],
1440	        document["tip"],
1441	    )
1442	    digest = hashlib.sha256(message).digest()
1443	    if not crypto.verify_signature(pinned, digest, attestation["signature"]):
1444	        raise _Failure(ERR_INTEGRITY)
